Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
description:
arXiv:2611.21847v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. However, increasing the number of agents or iterations does not automatically translate to producing more diverse or feasible ideas. Agents may converge on similar candidates, propagate unsupported claims through shared memory components and repeatedly apply search strategies that no longer yield any improvements.

title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
description:
arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. description:
arXiv:2611.22179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic memory research has accumulated extraction, supersession, reflection, and graph synthesis on top of retrieval-augmented generation. description:
arXiv:2611.21964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulators based on partial differential equations (PDEs) are widely used to model physical systems, but generating and interpreting PDE solver code with large language models (LLMs) remains challenging. description:
arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
description:
arXiv:2611.22102v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
description:
arXiv:2611.22115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
description:
arXiv:2611.22131v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder.

title: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
description:
arXiv:2611.22148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Open-weight language models are widely observed to get worse the longer they generate. Often, attempts to fix this involve more training. At high temperature, The sampler, i.e. the rule that picks the next token out of the model's probabilities, decides whether long and agentic generation survives and/or thrives. title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
description:
arXiv:2611.22177v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents are tested on news, but news reaches stock prices within minutes, and a benchmark that replays headlines at their publication time finds no alpha in trading on them. Money can then remain in two places, before news whose date is known, such as earnings announcements, and after bad news, if the market's fall went too far. title: The Fragility of Reasoning-Importance Attribution for Pruning Language Models
description:
arXiv:2611.22234v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attribution-guided pruning scores components by their causal contribution and protects the important ones, and it is increasingly applied to compress reasoning language models without destroying their chain of thought. Its reliability rests on an unexamined assumption: that reasoning importance can be faithfully measured. Across four small reasoning models, we show this measurement is fragile in three ways, each of which changes pruning decisions.

title: Context Has a Price: Adding and Removing Context for LLM Coding Agents under Prefix Caching
description:
arXiv:2611.22238v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents repeatedly send their conversation history to a language model. Adding useful code may reduce search, while removing old tool outputs may shorten later prompts. But do these changes reduce the cost of solving a task? We study this as a measurement problem in more than 20,000 runs of open models on SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench and Loc-Bench. title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
description:
arXiv:2611.22245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent delegation lets LLM systems distribute evidence collection across workers with separate contexts. This creates a consistency challenge: facts retrieved by workers may be missing from the evidence available to the lead for a joint conclusion. title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
description:
arXiv:2611.21958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator.
